name: Pupils per synthetic cohort
range: 40,000 in the principal sweep and paired tutoring-choice runs; 151,000 in the 2026 school-structure model
description: The standalone Python function defaults to 60,000. Synthetic cohort size is distinct from an observed pupil count.

name: Random seed
range: Varies by run; principal design seed root 27112026
description: Each cohort seed generates separate random streams for population, school and exam stages.

name: Starting ability and family wealth
description: Correlation between latent talent and log wealth.

name: Neighborhood wealth and family wealth
description: Controls how strongly a family’s synthetic wealth follows its assigned junior school zone.

name: Learning advantage linked to home resources
basis: SD per wealth SD; assumed and identified as a key driver.
description: Home-input contribution to initial skill per SD of log wealth.

name: Number of junior schools
description: Three hundred synthetic junior school zones receive standardized wealth draws.

name: Junior classes per school
description: Pupils are assigned randomly to a junior class within their school.

name: Variation in junior teacher effects
basis: SD units; literature range cited in register is 0.17–0.50 SD.
description: SD of teacher effects in junior schools; copied to HS_TEACH_SD for high schools.

name: Junior teacher advantage in richer zones
basis: SD per SD of zone wealth; assumed.
description: Junior teacher-quality gradient per SD of zone wealth.

name: Public academic-track places
basis: Share; upper end widened so the author-compiled 2026 figure (101,720 seats / about 151,000 candidates = 67.4%) is inside the sweep. Private entrants can raise the final academic share above this.
description: Share of cohort initially assigned a public academic-track place before private/exit handling.

name: Selective high-school places
range: 10% in the principal sweep; changes with academic capacity in the era sensitivity
description: Share of all pupils eligible for a selective high-school seat. This is a separate admissions stage from the university proxy.

name: School-based share of selective high-school places
basis: Share; official-rules motivated, but the sweep includes values below the stated 50% minimum (see rule mismatch below).
description: Fraction of the model’s elite-seat pool reserved for school-based zhibiao allocation, among local-hukou eligible academic pupils.

name: Number of public high schools
range: 60 stylized public schools; 2026 school-structure scenario uses a campus roster
description: Public academic secondary schools in the stylized model.

name: Target senior class size
description: Pupils are grouped into roughly balanced classes using an integer school size divided by the target.

name: Learning gain from a regular public high school
basis: SD; literature range of 0–0.20 widened to 0–0.50.
description: School value added per regular tier; elite tier receives twice this amount in the code.

name: Share of pupils in a high school’s top band
description: Per school, rank pupils and assign the top eighth to the top band, rounded with a minimum of one.

name: Extra teaching benefit in the top band
basis: Model score units; motivated by Wu et al. (2019), not a fitted interval.
description: Cumulative two-stage teaching premium; half applied per stage.

name: Extra peer benefit in the top band
basis: Model score units; default total 0.44. Broad independent ranges are sensitivity choices.
description: Cumulative two-stage peer premium; half applied per stage.

name: Variation in senior teacher effects
range: Linked to junior teacher SD in the sampled analysis, 0.15–0.45
description: Controls variation of senior class teacher effects. The standalone reference is 0.20.

name: Senior learning linked to starting ability
description: A senior-school skill increment of 0.5 model score units per latent talent unit.

name: Share of early advantages that fades
basis: Fraction; unmeasured and flagged as highly influential.
description: Fraction of the pre-gate “head start” that fades by the later high-school stage. One common fade rate applies to home, junior-school teacher, and pre-gate tutoring components.

name: Reassign classes in senior year two
range: On and off in saved comparisons
description: The model may reassign senior-year classes using a weighted composite of original entrance ranking and interim performance.

name: Exam score noise
basis: SD; assumed. A common magnitude is reused across exams.
description: SD of exam measurement noise, used at zhongkao, interim high-school observation, and gaokao.

name: Share without Guangzhou household registration
description: Fraction of the synthetic cohort without local hukou.

name: Wealth shift for families without local registration
description: Additive mean wealth shift for non-hukou families.

name: Junior-school teacher effect for nonlocals
basis: SD; assumed; register cites private-school VA near zero.
description: Junior-school teacher-quality penalty for non-hukou pupils, standing in for minban or purchased-place schooling.

name: Cap on nonlocal public and selective admissions
basis: Share; rules cited as 8–15% core districts, 8–18% outer districts, and 8–20% from 2027. The sweep reaches beyond the stated 2026 outer-district upper bound.
description: Maximum non-hukou fraction used for public academic seats and, separately, for the elite tier.

name: Annual private-school fee
description: Annual private high-school fee in yuan. Code checks whether it is strictly below the stated allowed share of modeled income.

name: Income share allowed for private-school fees
description: The private-school fee must fall below 40% of annual modeled household income. This is separate from the revised tutoring budget.

name: Reference annual household income
description: Income equals the reference value times exp(0.7 × log wealth). The resulting cohort median and upper tail vary.

name: Number of private high schools
range: 12 in the stylized design; roster used in the 2026 structure scenario
description: Number of private school groups. The stylized default has no separate count cap on private seats.

name: Entrance-score floor for school-based quota
basis: Share; assumed, described as consistent with 2026 rules.
description: Minimum score threshold for zhibiao eligibility, expressed as the top fraction of the full synthetic cohort.

name: Pre-entrance tutoring scale without restrictions
basis: Share scale; practitioner check; assumption and CIEFR 2017 survey (38.1%) cited.
description: Wealth-weighted probability scale for pre-gate tutoring absent the ban.

name: Reduction in early tutoring
basis: Sensitivity assumption; household trends do not identify this effect.
description: Central effective tutoring reduction before the wealth gradient.

name: How restriction changes with wealth
basis: Assumed coefficient, motivated by Liu et al. (2024), Liu and Bray (2025), and Yang (2026). None estimates this range.
description: Wealth gradient in effective restriction, increasing reduction among poorer pupils.

name: Pre-entrance tutoring gain
basis: SD; judgment anchored to null, small or negative findings (Zhang Y. 2013; Zhang L. 2024; Zhang Z. et al. 2025). No source gives these bounds; negative values are not sampled.
description: Initial-skill gain for a pupil taking pre-gate tutoring.

name: Weight on new performance when classes are reassigned
description: Weight on observed senior-1 performance versus zhongkao rank in senior-2 class assignment.

name: Boarding or day-school scenario
range: Boarding or day school in stylized runs
description: Day schools triple the term tutoring probability scale. The separate school-roster scenario uses school bed capacity ratios.

name: Term tutoring participation scale
basis: Share scale; practitioner check and author observation, uncertain.
description: Baseline term tutoring take-up scale for academic pupils when boarding (both skill-distribution tails); tripled when BOARD=False.

name: Holiday tutoring participation scale
description: Baseline holiday tutoring take-up scale (both tails), before wealth/skill weighting.

name: Effect of one senior tutoring episode
basis: SD per episode; same literature and caveat as PRE_EFF. Stress values 0.20 and 0.40 are run in mechanisms.py.
description: Gaokao-skill gain per term or holiday tutoring episode.

name: Target for full-time outside study
basis: Share; assumption informed by a practitioner check; denominator unconfirmed.
description: Target share of the whole cohort in full-time outside-institution study while retaining a school place.

name: Annual full-time small-group tuition
description: Annual assumed small-group price. Legacy affordability requires the fee to be below half of modeled household income.

name: Full-time tutoring gain before accounting for displaced school
basis: SD; sign unknown. Pupils in this route lose modeled in-school teacher and peer effects.
description: Gaokao-skill effect of full-time institution study relative to school-class effects.

name: Tutoring demand when achievement trails wealth rank
basis: Behavioral coefficient; assumed approximation of assumed mechanism.
description: Strength of tutoring response to a positive gap between family wealth rank and pupil skill rank (“fear of falling”).

name: Classmate influence on tutoring demand
description: Strength of one-round peer escalation in classmates’ tutoring take-up.

name: Target share on art-exam route
description: Target share of cohort taking the art-exam route; selection is weighted toward wealthier and lower-skill academic pupils.

name: Art-exam score advantage proxy
basis: SD; assumption that the specialist exam is easier; assumed scale.
description: Additive effective-score advantage for art route.

name: Target share on joint-exam route
description: Target share of cohort using the Hong Kong/Macau/Taiwan joint-exam route; selected from the wealthiest academic pupils.

name: Joint-exam score advantage proxy
basis: SD; assumption of easier entry; assumed scale.
description: Additive effective-score advantage for the joint-exam route.

name: Selective high-school seats reserved for purchase
description: Inactive option retained for a Hong Kong comparison, assigning part of the selective capacity by wealth.

name: Neighborhood weight in selective admission
description: Inactive option retained for a Hong Kong comparison, adding a neighborhood score weight for open selective entry.

name: Correlation of cognitive and noncognitive skills
description: Target association of starting cognitive and noncognitive skills. No pupil data calibrate it.

name: Noncognitive skill and family wealth
description: Target association between noncognitive skill and modeled log wealth.

name: Weight on noncognitive skill in senior learning
description: Senior-high gain per unit of noncognitive skill. The paper’s main sweep sets this to zero.

name: School-level data option
description: If enabled, school plans, beds, ownership and cutoff order affect assignment. The data are provisional and 61 cutoffs are imputed.

name: Reference size of the entrance-exam cohort
description: About 151,000 entrance-exam candidates are used for scaling school capacity.

name: Reference number of academic places
range: 101,720 in the 2026 scenario; roughly 20%–43% of 151,000 in the stylized 2000 scenario
description: The model rescales the compiled campus plan total of 104,584 to this reference figure. The two totals differ.

name: Local wealth threshold for removing tutoring purchases
description: Removes tutoring and full-time study for families above the local 60th wealth percentile. Comparisons can hold placements fixed or recompute them.

name: Change in tutoring gains with family wealth
description: Tutoring effects are multiplied by 1 + slope × (2 × wealth rank − 1). Positive slope gives richer pupils larger returns.

name: Target reduction in expected early take-up
description: Uses a numerical solver to reach a fixed average expected reduction in early tutoring so different wealth gradients are comparable.

name: Reduction in term tutoring probability
description: Multiplies baseline modeled post-gate term tutoring probability by one minus this cut.

name: Reduction in holiday tutoring probability
description: Multiplies baseline modeled holiday tutoring probability by one minus this cut.

name: Multiplier on school boarding capacity
description: Multiplies the bed-to-plan ratio used as an input to synthetic boarding status. Capacity and actual occupancy can differ.

name: Share of private places filled
description: Share of the private-seat plan filled before checking uptake. The reported 2025 completion rate was 60.4%.

name: How synthetic pupils and wealth are generated
value: Normal zone and individual wealth draws
description: Pupils are assigned uniformly to junior zones. Household log wealth adds a zone component, an independent normal residual and a nonlocal shift. No pupil microdata are fitted.

name: Wealth-to-income multiplier
description: Annual income is the reference value times exp(0.7 × log wealth). Household assets and cash buffers are omitted.

name: How starting ability is generated
value: Wealth component plus independent normal residual
description: Latent ability includes TAL_WEALTH times log wealth and a scaled residual. It is unobserved in the real school records. Noncognitive skill shares an ability residual so joint correlations can be constructed.

name: Junior teacher assignments by registration
value: Assigned school-class draw for locals; separate draw for nonlocals
description: Locals share a class-level teacher effect; nonlocals receive separate draws centered at minus the modeled penalty. Real schools use more varied arrangements.

name: How the early head start is built
value: Junior teacher + home contribution + early tutoring
range: Common fade rate in saved runs
description: Starting test skill is initial talent plus the modeled head start. The exam adds independent Gaussian noise. One fade rate applies to all three sources of early advantage.

name: Early tutoring rule in the original model
range: Fixed shape; scale and restriction vary
description: Before enforcement the probability is PRE_SHARE × 2 × wealth rank, clipped at one. The cut is BAN_RED × (1 + BAN_GRAD × (1 − 2 × wealth rank)), clipped between zero and one.

name: Public and private high-school allocation
value: Public ordering by entrance score under nonlocal quota
description: In the stylized model, high-scoring nonlocals blocked by the public quota can buy a private place if affordable, else exit. The roster variant allows families that meet the threshold to compete for finite private places. Remaining pupils do not enter the academic track.

name: Who gets school-based selective places
value: Local academic pupils above a cohort-wide minimum
description: The school-based pool is divided proportionally across junior schools using their eligible academic pupils, rounded and filled by score. Open admission uses the remaining seats and separate nonlocal cap. Actual criteria vary.

name: High-school sorting and school premiums
value: Twice regular added value in selective public schools
description: Pupils are assigned by score order to selective, regular public and private schools. Private pupils get no public-school value-added term in this construction.

name: Teacher and peer advantage across two stages
value: Half the cumulative premium per stage
description: Stage 1 and stage 2 each give half of the cumulative teaching and peer premium to pupils in that stage’s top band. A pupil in both receives the full cumulative amount.

name: How later skill is assembled
value: Retained head start + talent-related growth + school terms
description: School value added and class effects are added to initial talent, the retained early advantage and talent-related growth. The optional noncognitive term appears only in senior high school.

name: Separate school-by-class teacher effects
description: Class-level teacher draws use stable school-class indices. Without re-banding, the first-stage class and teacher draws carry forward.

name: Which academic pupils are likelier to seek tutoring
value: 2× below the 20th or above the 80th skill percentile; 0.5× between
description: Multiplies these skill weights by 0.5 + family wealth rank. Demand also responds to a positive gap between family wealth rank and pupil skill rank. Nonacademic pupils are excluded.

name: Feedback from classmates’ demand
description: Final uptake probabilities depend on average predicted classmate uptake. They are clipped to a probability range. This is not a market equilibrium.

name: Who takes full-time outside schooling in the original model
value: Academic pupils below median academic skill and price below half of income
description: Draw randomly among eligible candidates up to the target. Their final school teacher and peer terms are replaced by a full-time learning term. The legacy rules can still count term and holiday episodes.

name: Art route selection
value: Weight = wealth rank squared × (1.5 − skill rank)
description: Sample within the academic track after the joint-exam selection. Pupils receive at most one route bonus, applied to the effective exam ranking.

name: Hong Kong Macao Taiwan joint-exam selection
value: Academic pupils above the 70th wealth percentile
description: The sampled joint-exam route is a proxy. Actual citizenship, exam eligibility and separately allocated capacities are not implemented.

name: Selective university outcome
value: 10% of the full cohort, filled from the academic track
description: Admission is based on final effective score. The original code admits all tied at the cutoff, and the principal sweep tests capacity. Alternative routes change who enters the pool.

name: Government subsidy accounting proxy
value: Six primary, three junior, and three senior years
description: Primary local/nonlocal ¥19,600/¥5,000 annually; junior ¥32,100/¥6,000; senior public academic ¥41,500, other modeled school route ¥38,400, private or exit ¥0. Subsidies do not affect admissions.

name: Original five-year spending proxy
value: ¥45,000 early, ¥35,080 senior term, ¥20,000 senior holiday, twice annual full-time fee
description: Multiply each participation indicator by this amount and add. Assumes early purchases for three years and senior purchases for two years. This differs from the annual revised choice model.

name: Who counts as poorer, richer and high ability
value: Local wealth bottom/top 40% or 10%; full cohort top 5%, 10% or 20% of latent talent
description: The conditional opportunity rate is a university proxy among these pupils. Local registration and latent starting ability are explicit analytical restrictions.

name: Definitions of the three wealth comparisons
value: Rich-to-poor admission rates within comparable groups
range: Score and ability bins; joint support reported
description: Score and ability comparisons average rates within 10 bins in the corresponding top quintile. Joint comparison uses five score by five ability bins within the top score quintile; retain cells with at least five rich and five poor pupils and report pooled support.

name: Rank bands for the displacement experiment
description: Ranks use the full simulated cohort and final effective score. A move down a band does not necessarily mean losing university proxy admission.

name: Principal sampling design
description: Ranges define the design rather than empirical probability distributions for Guangzhou. The experiment uses matched exam and cohort draws for paired contrasts.

name: What changes in the restriction and class-policy contrasts
description: The combined arm changes both early tutoring restriction and later class re-banding. The isolated arm changes only early tutoring restriction. Neither estimates a causal effect of Double Reduction.

name: School roster data and policy ranges
description: Uses observed cutoff ordering where available and ownership medians where missing. Principal ranges include school-quota values below 50% and nonlocal cap values above some cited 2026 district limits.

name: Approximate 2000 and 2017 scenarios
value: 2026 institutions held fixed; selected take-up, bedding and place settings changed
description: These sensitivity runs use the same school roster, policies and final university proxy capacity across eras. Circa 2000 academic places vary between 20% and 43% of the cohort.

name: Excluded long-run outcomes and household costs
value: University outcome proxy ends the main model
description: Vocational education quality, employment, tuition and dorm costs for public high school, and non-monetary costs of long boarding days are excluded.

name: Scenario identifier
range: Saved case names from 40 revised arms
description: Each saved run has its own named scenario. The central case uses middle grades and a 0.18 SD gain and belief reference.

name: Grade 9 market context
description: The two contexts have different annual purchase intercepts. Comparing contexts does not isolate a policy effect.

name: Grade 9 annual participation target
description: After-policy targets are 15%, 25%, 35%; before-policy targets 35%, 45%, 55%. These are model targets for a held-out pilot, not city estimates.

name: Grade 11 annual participation target
description: Targets among academic-track pupils are 20%, 30%, 40%. This target is independent of the Grade 9 policy scenario.

name: Realized tutoring gain
description: Expected mean true gain before dose, quality and pupil response. The 0.75 and 1.00 SD scenarios stress the response. Published anchors use other settings and populations.

name: Public expectation of tutoring gains
description: The shared signal enters perception alongside format-specific noise and a common prior. It can vary independently from the realized gain.

name: Grade 9 realized gain override
description: Keeps Grade 9 gain at the middle reference when isolating a Grade 11 learning change.

name: Grade 9 belief signal override
description: Keeps Grade 9 beliefs at the middle reference when isolating a Grade 11 expectation change.

name: Share of household income available for tutoring
description: One annual cutoff for a pupil’s chosen package across seasons. The model does not deduct rent, food and other expenses or model borrowing, siblings, assets or carryover.

name: Part-time fee multiplier
description: Scales the assumed ¥110 hourly group and ¥250 hourly individual prices at a given quality scenario.

name: Full-time small-group annual price
description: Cost of the term-only replacement option, corresponding to ¥60,000–¥80,000 per semester.

name: Premium one-to-one annual price
description: The reference extends ¥100,000 a month across twelve months. Lower stress prices use ten months. Several premium arms combine price with the 80% budget assumption.

name: Premium quality multiplier
description: Scales both perceived and realized package effects for premium tutoring. Its distance from average tutoring quality is unmeasured.

name: Part-time group quality multiplier
description: A two-thirds arm proxies a larger-class quality penalty. The model has no observed relationship between group size and benefit.

name: Provider availability multiplier
description: Multiplies season- and format-specific supplier probabilities. No access is a paired control.

name: Weekly part-time package multiplier
description: Raises hours, price and the minimum usable time window together. Weekly defaults are two hours for group and one-and-a-half for individual.

name: Boarders’ weekly usable term time
description: Shorter windows prevent booking a package that requires a larger block. Day pupils have a fixed four-hour modeled window.

name: Grade 11 boarding allocation rule
range: Random or ranked by entrance score
description: Selects the same 78% share under each rule. Grade 9 boarding remains a random 12%.

name: Direct effect of wealth rank on tutoring preference
description: Adds the coefficient times the difference between household wealth rank and 0.5. Zero leaves the affordability channel and all other covariates in place.

name: Force no tutoring purchases
description: If enabled every household chooses the no-purchase option. Ordinary school inputs are retained.

name: Share of Grade 9 learning gains that fades
description: Uses the original fade mechanism with paired no-tutoring controls. The carried Grade 9 tutoring term fades with other early inputs.

name: Grades and populations modeled
description: Grade 9 covers the full incoming cohort. Grade 11 covers the academic track after high-school placement, including public and private academic schools. Other routes remain in the full-cohort denominator.

name: Annual tutoring formats and seasons
value: None, part-time group, part-time individual, full-time small group, premium one-to-one
description: Part-time packages can combine any nonempty group of three seasons, within one format. Both full-time modes are term-only and cannot coexist with another package.

name: Number of modeled weeks per season
description: These modeled seasons build annual amounts. Participation is the union of the seasonal indicators.

name: Part-time weekly package sizes
description: Each selected season requires enough weekly time for the whole package. The price is per hour × weekly hours × weeks booked.

name: Part-time baseline prices
description: All prices describe hypothetical packages. There is no modeled supply curve or firm response to demand.

name: Modeled boarding prevalence
range: Fixed shares; alternative G11 allocation rule
description: Grade 9 status is independently drawn for each pupil. Academic Grade 11 seats are allocated by sampled random keys or entrance rank.

name: Time windows by term and holiday
value: Day 4/12/8 hours; boarder 1/8/6 hours per week
range: Boarding term can expand to 3 hours
description: Numbers are ordered term/summer/winter. A package fits only if each of its booked seasons has enough time. Full-time options replace the school day and bypass this after-school window.

name: Seasonal seller probabilities
range: Individual 10 percentage points below group; clipped after multiplier
description: Term/summer/winter probability is matched by season and format. Full-time base access is 30% small group and 20% premium among affordable eligible households.

name: How families form effectiveness expectations
value: 70% current signal + 30% prior of 0.08 SD + normal noise
range: Format-level noise SD 0.065; truncated at zero
description: Families see prior performance signals and first-year band, with noise. Future pupil-specific outcomes are unavailable to their choice decision.

name: Expected learning, price and time in package utility
description: Adds a tail/remediation preference, wealth-rank preference, season taste and format preference relative to no tutoring. Deducts 0.0015 × annual hours for part-time; 0.25 for full-time group and 0.40 for premium.

name: Remediation and extension preferences
value: 0.25 × 2 × distance from middle skill rank + 0.14 × positive wealth-achievement gap
description: Demand can rise for pupils at either end of the prior achievement distribution. The wealth-achievement term applies only when family wealth rank exceeds the pupil’s skill rank.

name: Random tastes and prior score signals
value: Format Gumbel scale 0.55; season normal SD 0.12; prior score normal SD 0.25
description: Season tastes add over selected periods. A household chooses the best feasible package only if its utility plus the grade-level intercept is positive relative to no purchase.

name: Expected and realized school displacement
value: 100% of current teacher/peer inputs replaced by either full-time format
range: No current school displacement for part-time
description: Families anticipate 0.05 school units plus 0.16 for a first-year top-band pupil, then normalize to the no-tutoring score scale. Accounting subtracts the actual modeled current teacher and peer terms. Enrollment, earlier school input, placements and other routes remain.

name: How tutoring hours become a learning dose
value: Part-time annual hours ÷ 88, capped at 1.5×; full-time dose 1×
description: Package prices and schedule account for all chosen hours. Realized gross effects use the matched no-tutoring score scale. Grade 9 scale uses all pupils and Grade 11 scale uses academic-track pupils.

name: Pupil-level variation in realized gains
description: Multiply the reference gain by dose, format quality, matched scale and unseen pupil-level realization. A zero true gain can still leave a negative net shift in full-time replacement.

name: Annual participation brackets
range: Reference bands are fixed; observed results vary across matched seeds
description: The Grade 9 brackets use descriptive research as context. Grade 11 brackets are independently stipulated. These are assumed ranges rather than named surveys’ city-grade estimates.

name: Participation intercepts by modeled grade and context
range: Low, middle and high per context
description: Intercepts come from the price-adjusted best-offer utility distribution for 8,000 pilot pupils, seed 472001. They were frozen before eight definitive cohorts.

name: Matched tutoring-choice experiment
range: 336 result rows including two legacy benchmarks
description: Each contrast shares pupil population and random draws where applicable. Seeds and grade differentiate latent choice streams. The 40 study settings do not span every combination.

name: Fixed-placement effect of removing tutoring
value: Family wealth at or above local 60th percentile
description: Schools, class assignment, academic enrollment and exam-route bonuses stay fixed. The net version restores any displaced current school inputs.

name: Household budgets and the limits of the price sensitivity
value: One income-based cap per pupil and modeled year
range: Assumed cap and synthetic income distribution
description: Actual available cash, taxes, essential spending, credit, scholarships, siblings and multi-year financial decisions are excluded.
